title: Partner Co-sell / Pipeline Review - Lumos Partners
summary: Weekly co-sell pipeline sync to align on prioritized joint deals, review technical blockers for two P1 opportunities, confirm next steps for joint outreach and technical deep dive scheduling.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated co-sell deck and joint ICP by 2026-12-23
Schedule technical deep-dive with Lumos SEs week of 2026-12-27 (Marcus to propose times)
Customer to prioritize top 5 deals in spreadsheet and flag buyer personas by 2026-12-24
Redwood to share security pack (SOC 2 + KMS whitepaper) via Confluence link by 2026-12-23
action_items: Ava Martinez: Send co-sell deck and one-pager by 2026-12-23
Marcus Lee: Run latency checklist and share preliminary numbers for P1 deals by 2026-12-29
Sofia Ramos: Update pipeline sheet with champion contact details for top 5 by 2026-12-24
Priya Nair: Confirm internal SEs for technical deep dive and share constraints by 2026-12-23
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-12-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Recording: Yes
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava, AE on the Redwood partner motion. Marcus from our SE team is here as well.
[00:08] Sofia Ramos: Hi Ava, hi Marcus, thanks  Sofia from Lumos. Ethan and Priya are on as well.
[00:12] Ethan Cole: Hey all, quick note, we had a last-minute calendar shift so apologies if we start a little tight on time.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: No worries. Quick agenda: prioritize pipeline, call out technical risks (latency / auth), and agree on next steps for co-sell outreach.
[00:33] Sofia Ramos: Sounds good. We uploaded the latest pipeline  there are 8 joint opportunities, two P1s we want to focus on: Acera Health and Meridian Logistics.
[00:45] Ava Martinez: Great. For context, do you have champions and timelines on those two?
[00:52] Sofia Ramos: Acera is Q1 close, champion is Jill (Director of Innovation). Meridian is more complex, looks like a Q2 earliest, champion is Tom in ops.
[01:05] Ethan Cole: For Meridian we have a security review coming up  they require SOC 2 plus an on-prem option for some workloads mentioned in the RFP.
[01:15] Marcus Lee: Okay that's notable. Our Private deployment supports VPC and on-prem packaging; there can be some lead time for HSM/KMS integrations. We'll call out expected timelines.
[01:28] Priya Nair: Can you remind us about encryption at rest with Redwood  is customer-managed KMS supported? The RFP explicitly asks for CMK support.

[01:36] Ava Martinez: Yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM options in Private; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations. I'll send the security pack after this call.
[01:50] Sofia Ramos: Perfect  that'll help Meridian. For Acera, the ask is lower latency and predictable SLA. They run real-time triage workflows so latency variance is a concern.

[02:05] Marcus Lee: Understood. We should run a quick latency sim for their sequence length and token rates. There are a few levers: Dedicated pools, KV caching, and quantization settings. I can prototype an estimate by next week.
[02:20] Ethan Cole: When you say Dedicated pools  do you mean Redwood Dedicated where we reserve GPUS? Their procurement team asks about commit sizing and burst behavior.

[02:29] Marcus Lee: Right, Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity with burst options. We'll propose a small reserved commit and burst for peak hours; I'll include throughput numbers per instance type.
[02:40] Sofia Ramos: Any concerns about model compatibility? Acera wants to use a proprietary LLM they're experimenting with  will Redwood support custom model onboarding in Dedicated or Private?

[02:52] Ava Martinez: We onboard customer models for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has curated catalog. There are security reviews and kernel optimization steps but it's a supported path. Marcus can detail the steps.

[03:05] Marcus Lee: The flow is: model artifacts collection (weights + config), compatibility check (ops/arch), small benchmark run to verify latency and memory, then rollout profile. For proprietary models we usually recommend Private for data and IP protection.
[03:20] Priya Nair: That aligns with what Meridian will ask. For the benchmark run, do you need a dataset or can you run synthetic sequences?
[03:29] Marcus Lee: Synthetic is fine to start  ideally we get a few sample prompts to mirror distribution. If they can share a small redacted prompt set that helps accuracy and tail-latency checks.
[03:40] Ava Martinez: Action: Sofia to try and get a few sample prompts from both Acera and Meridian. Marcus to run latency checklist once samples arrive.
[03:50] Sofia Ramos: Will do. One other thing  co-sell crediting and ownership: Lumos wants clarity on outreach sequences and which account team own lines to avoid duplication.

[04:00] Ava Martinez: Good point. Proposal: Redwood owns the technical outreach and initial demo, Lumos owns the commercial intro and executive sponsor engagement. We log all interactions in the joint CRM sheet so ownership is clear.
[04:15] Ethan Cole: Works for us. We'll flag the primary owner column in the spreadsheet. Also, can Redwood provide a one-pager for AE handoff with positioning and objection handling?
[04:25] Ava Martinez: Yes, I'll attach a one-pager with battlecards. We'll include common objections like latency vs cost tradeoffs and Dedicated vs Hosted guidance.

[04:35] Marcus Lee: Quick technical note  for Acera's low-latency requirement, we might recommend token-level caching for repetitive prefixes and lower quantization to hit latency SLOs. That will impact cost slightly; we'll show numbers.
[04:48] Sofia Ramos: Sounds reasonable. On procurement side, Meridian asked about audit logs and RBAC  they want per-team RBAC and immutable audit logs for model access.

[04:58] Marcus Lee: We support RBAC and audit logs in the Console; audit retention is configurable as an add-on. For immutable logs we can work with them on the retention policy and S3/partner archiving.
[05:12] Priya Nair: Great. Also, is there any known limitation for on-prem packages around GPU types? Meridian's infra team uses older Ampere instances.
[05:22] Marcus Lee: On-prem has some constraints; older Ampere is generally fine but for optimized kernels we prefer newer drivers. We'll include a compatibility matrix in the technical deep dive.

[05:35] Ava Martinez: Recap: we'll send co-sell deck + one-pager, security pack, and Marcus will run latency checks once prompt samples are provided. Sofia to prioritize pipeline and get sample prompts. Everyone ok with dates in the action items?
[05:50] Sofia Ramos: Yes, dates look good. One wrinkle: Acera wants a joint pilot with a 2-week POC; budget ok but they need a tight SOW. Can Redwood do a 2-week POC on Dedicated trial?

[06:04] Ava Martinez: We can support a short pilot; usually it's easier on Hosted for a quick turn-up, but if they need dedicated isolation we can spin up a small Dedicated pool for the pilot. We'll outline scope and pricing in the SOW.
[06:18] Ethan Cole: Procurement will need a sample SOW and pricing tiers. Can you share a template?
[06:23] Ava Martinez: Yes, I'll attach a sample SOW with typical pilot pricing and escalation path.
[06:32] Priya Nair: For the technical deep dive week of 12/27, any preferred time slots? We are in PST, so mornings are best.
[06:40] Marcus Lee: I'm flexible; I'll propose Tue/Wed morning PST in the calendar invite.
[06:46] Sofia Ramos: Quick question  you mentioned KV cache earlier. Does Redwood have autoscaling for cache hit warmups? We've seen cold start latency issues in other platforms.
[06:56] Marcus Lee: We have prefix/KV caching and warmup hooks; autoscaling can be tuned and we can do pre-warm scripts as part of the pilot to reduce cold start tail latency.
[07:06] Ava Martinez: I'm going to drop the security docs link in chat now (see attachments).
[07:10] [link posted] https://redwood.com/security/lumos-security-pack.pdf
[07:15] Ethan Cole: Got it, thanks. One final thing from our side: are you able to support SAML SSO integrations with our customers quickly or is that a longer lead?
[07:25] Ava Martinez: SAML SSO is standard for Private and Dedicated customers; hosted customers can use SAML with some configuration. I'll include the integration checklist in the security pack.
[07:35] Sofia Ramos: Ok great. Anything else on the pipeline?
[07:38] Ethan Cole: We had a question about co-funding for joint events  do you have a marketing budget for joint webinars or trade shows?
[07:46] Ava Martinez: Yes, we have a modest co-marketing fund for strategic partners; let's flag opportunities in the sheet and we can work through approvals.
[07:55] Sofia Ramos: Awesome. If no other blockers, let's recap next steps and owners.

[08:00] Ava Martinez: Recap: 1) Ava to send co-sell deck, one-pager, SOW template, and security pack by 2026-12-23. 2) Sofia to prioritize and add champion contacts + sample prompts by 2026-12-24. 3) Marcus to run latency checklist and propose Dedicated sizing + throughput numbers by 2026-12-29. 4) Schedule technical deep dive week of 12/27  Marcus to propose times.
[08:20] Priya Nair: Confirmed. We'll look out for the materials and update the sheet this week.
[08:25] Ava Martinez: Thanks everyone  we'll follow up with the materials and get the deep dive on the calendar.
[08:30] Sofia Ramos: Thanks Ava, Marcus. Talk soon.
[08:33] Meeting end.
